failures.title: BMW B47D20A Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: EGR Cooler Failure and Coolant Leaks - 2014-Present
items.whatHappens: The EGR cooler can develop internal micro-fractures, allowing coolant to seep into the intake or exhaust system. This often presents as unexplained coolant loss, white exhaust smoke, or in severe cases, a potential fire risk if coolant enters the EGR module's electrical components.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, an EGR cooler replacement or system blanking (where legally compliant) is sufficient. However, if the engine has suffered hydrolock from severe coolant ingress, a full B47D20A engine replacement is the only viable option.

items.title: Timing Chain and Tensioner Wear - 2014-Present
items.whatHappens: While vastly improved over the catastrophic rear-chain design of the N47, the B47's front-mounted timing chain can still stretch over high mileages. Symptoms include a faint rattling noise on cold starts, though it is far less frequent and less severe than its predecessor.
items.repairVsReplace: A timing chain kit replacement is a straightforward, preventative maintenance task on the B47 due to its accessible front-end design. Full engine replacement is rarely required solely for chain wear unless neglected for an extreme period.

failures.goodYearsLine: The B47D20A is widely considered a robust and reliable modern diesel. Post-2018 updates further refined the EGR and cooling systems, making later G-generation hosts exceptionally durable with proper maintenance .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the B47D20A
variants.intro: The B47D20A engine code is stamped directly onto the engine block, typically located on a machined pad near the oil filter housing or on the front timing cover. It is also explicitly listed on your vehicle's V5C registration document under the engine details section, or it can be definitively verified via a VIN decode through a BMW specialist. The B47D20A is frequently confused with the older N47D20C or the higher-output B47D20B. While they share similar physical dimensions, fitting the wrong revision can result in ECU mapping conflicts, incompatible turbo plumbing, and different oil filter housing mounts. Always verify the exact code before purchasing a replacement unit.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement B47D20A - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used B47D20A is a viable budget option for this engine, provided it comes with comprehensive service history proving the EGR cooler was inspected or replaced preventatively. The front-mounted timing chain makes verifying its condition easier, but inheriting a neglected EGR system remains the primary risk.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned B47D20A is the most balanced choice for most owners. A reputable rebuild will replace the EGR cooler, turbocharger seals, and all critical gaskets with updated parts, directly addressing the engine's most common failure points while restoring factory compression.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is highly justified for the B47D20A due to its excellent repairability index and accessible front-end design. An upgraded rebuild should include a revised EGR setup, updated timing chain components, and potentially a remapped ECU to maximise longevity and performance.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting your B47D20A through our vetted network ensures the work is completed by BMW specialists, backed by a minimum 12-month warranty and nationwide delivery options.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: For typical host vehicles like the G20 3 Series or G01 X3, current market values range from £14,000 to £35,000. A reconditioned B47D20A replacement sits comfortably within this value band, making it a financially sound investment. Even for older F-generation hosts valued around £7,000, the lower labour hours required for B47 repairs often keep the total fitted cost below the scrap threshold.

items.answer: A reconditioned BMW B47D20A engine typically costs between £2,800 and £4,500 for supply only, with fitted prices ranging from £3,320 to £5,280. Used units start around £1,500 but may inherit EGR cooler or turbo wear. Fitted costs generally include 8-12 hours of labour at independent specialist rates. items.question: What is the most common problem with the B47D20A engine?
items.answer: The dominant failure is EGR cooler failure, where internal micro-fractures allow coolant to leak into the exhaust or intake system. Typical onset is between 60,000 and 120,000 miles. Symptoms include unexplained coolant loss, white exhaust smoke, or in severe cases, a potential fire risk. While the front-mounted timing chain is vastly improved over the older N47, it can still stretch at very high mileages.

items.question: Which BMW models use the B47D20A engine?
items.answer: The B47D20A was widely fitted across BMW's F and G-generation lineup, including the 1 Series, 2 Series, 3 Series, 4 Series, 5 Series, X1, X2, and X3. It commonly powered the 116d, 118d, 120d, 216d, 218d, 220d, 316d, 318d, 320d, and 520d badges from 2014 onwards. Always verify your specific chassis code and engine stamping before ordering a replacement unit.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned B47D20A engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned B47D20A is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the known EGR cooler vulnerabilities of this generation. A proper rebuild will replace the EGR cooler, turbocharger seals, and critical gaskets with updated parts, directly addressing the root cause of failure. A used engine inherits the exact same EGR and cooling system risks unless it comes with documented, recent preventative maintenance records.
